profile.reading: The building tagged at this location on South 7th Street in Montpelier, the seat of Bear Lake County in southeastern Idaho, is identified with The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints under the label Family History Center. The Church operates several thousand Family History Centers around the world, nearly all of them small public research rooms housed inside local meetinghouses and staffed by volunteers, where visitors can use FamilySearch.org, microfilm and microfiche readers, and a handful of shared computers to research their family history free of charge. That is a materially different kind of building from a data center: a Family History Center is a patron facing reading room, not a facility built around server racks, structural floor loading for heavy equipment, or dedicated cooling and backup power infrastructure. No published source describes IT infrastructure, server capacity, or power specifications tied to this Bear Lake County location, and none would be expected, since these centers are not designed to house computing equipment beyond a few public terminals. This differs from the Church's well documented, purpose built digital preservation infrastructure elsewhere, such as the Granite Mountain Records Vault in Utah, which is a genuine large scale records storage facility and not the building associated with this address. This entry most likely reflects a mapping or classification error rather than an actual data center.

reading:
This entry is a tagging artefact, and the honest thing a registry can do with one is say so and show the working. The underlying record is an OpenStreetMap building in Bear Lake County, Idaho, named Family History Center, attributed to The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and carrying the map tag that marks a telecommunications data centre. The coordinates fall in Montpelier, and FamilySearch's own centre directory lists the Bear Lake Idaho FamilySearch Center at 661 Washington Street, Montpelier, Idaho 83254, closed on Wednesdays and Saturdays, open evenings by appointment for groups, and staffed by people trained to help visitors research their families.

A FamilySearch centre is a public genealogy research room. It gives walk in visitors access to record collections that cannot be viewed from home for licensing reasons, along with free use of subscription genealogy services and help from volunteers. The equipment is a small number of ordinary workstations, closer to a public library reference desk than to a server room. Nothing published describes computing infrastructure, backup power, cooling or network equipment at this address beyond that, and a county of a few thousand residents would not support any. The map tag is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that quietly inflates data centre counts wherever these records are aggregated without review.

The Church does operate serious records infrastructure, which is presumably how the confusion started, but not here. The Granite Mountain Records Vault, built in 1965 into the mountains near Salt Lake City, holds more than 3.5 billion images on microfilm, microfiche and digital media, gathered under agreements with archives, libraries and churches in more than 100 countries. The Church supplies copies back to the record custodians at no charge and has replaced collections lost in disasters. An ongoing programme converts the microfilm holdings to digital form for publication through FamilySearch. The vault itself is closed to the public for security reasons, and its detailed specifications are not published either.

This registry keeps the row rather than deleting it, for two reasons. The mistagging originates upstream in the open map data, so removing the row here would not correct the source and would only make the error invisible on the next import. And the same pattern has produced other false positives in this inventory, buildings tagged as data centres that are in fact laboratories, hiring offices and civic buildings, which is worth tracking as a class. The row is flagged for exclusion from capacity totals, and no capacity, floor area or infrastructure figure has been assigned to it.
